For my history coursework I'm comparing how newspapers covered school shootings in the 90s vs now. The difference is wild. Older coverage named the shooter in every headline and printed their photos everywhere. A lot of outlets now deliberately don't, because researchers found that coverage can inspire copycats.

I didn't know 'no notoriety' was an actual policy some newsrooms follow. Anyone know good books on media ethics around this? School library has nothing.
